finding.claim: With caching enabled, verify() given a Buffer token throws a TypeError before decoding, because the default cacheKeyBuilder (hashToken) calls String.prototype-only split() on the Buffer. Verification fails closed, so this is a reliability/error-handling defect, not an auth bypass.
finding.source: Caller-supplied token of type Buffer (accepted by the explicit type check at src/verifier.js:353) when the verifier is created with a cache option.
finding.sink: cache.get(cacheKeyBuilder(token)) at src/verifier.js:364, which calls hashToken at src/utils.js:46 (token.split on a Buffer).

trace.note: Buffer tokens pass the type check.
Cache lookup hashes the raw token before decode().
hashToken calls token.split('.', 1); Buffer has no split, so a TypeError is thrown.
decode() would have converted the Buffer to a string, but it is never reached.

finding.guards_checked: Type check at src/verifier.js:353 (accepts Buffer). Decoder Buffer handling at src/decoder.js:14-15 (not reached first). Cache is disabled by default (createCache returns null for undefined size, src/verifier.js:83-86), so the path requires an explicit cache option. Error is not a TokenError, so code-based handling in callers may not match it. Not a signature, claim, or algorithm bypass.
